text: Everyone online seems rich.
Twenty-somethings with paid-off houses. Thirty-year-olds retiring early. Your feed makes it look like everyone is miles ahead of you.
So let's look at what American families actually have, using the Federal Reserve's newest numbers.
By the end, you'll know exactly where you stand, and why you're probably not as behind as you feel.
First, a trap.
The Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances says the average American family is worth about one point two four million dollars.
A millionaire. The average family.
That sounds wrong, because it is misleading.
Picture ten regular people in a room. Then a billionaire walks in.
The average wealth in that room just exploded. But nobody else got a single dollar richer.
That's what averages do. A few very rich families drag the average way up.
So we use the median instead. Line every family up from poorest to richest, and pick the one in the exact middle.
The median American family is worth about two hundred sixteen thousand dollars.
Not one point two four million. Two hundred sixteen thousand.
And that number includes home equity, retirement accounts, cars, everything, minus all debt.
Now let's break it down by age, because comparing yourself to a sixty-year-old makes no sense.
Families under thirty-five: a median net worth of about thirty-three thousand dollars.
Thirty-five to forty-four: about one hundred fifty-six thousand.
Forty-five to fifty-four: about two hundred fifty-four thousand.
Fifty-five to sixty-four: about four hundred twelve thousand.
Sixty-five to seventy-four: about four hundred thirty-one thousand.
And seventy-five and older: about five hundred five thousand.
Notice the shape. Wealth is slow at first, and then it builds for decades.
And if you're under thirty-five and it feels harder lately, you're not imagining it.
The median net worth for families under thirty-five actually fell about twenty-three percent between 2022 and 2025.
So if you're young and your number looks small, you're looking at the start of the curve, not the end.
Now, cash. How much does the typical family keep in checking and savings?
The median is about eight thousand two hundred dollars.
Eight thousand. That's it. Not fifty thousand. Not a year of expenses.
So if you have even one month of expenses saved, you're doing better than a lot of people think.
Next, debt.
About forty-five percent of families carry a balance on their credit cards from month to month.
For those families, the median balance is about three thousand one hundred dollars.
And nearly one in five families said they'd been late on a loan payment in the past year. That's up from about one in eight in 2022.
So if you're juggling some debt, you have a lot of company. The goal isn't shame. The goal is a plan.
Then retirement.
Only about fifty-five percent of families have any retirement account at all. That's a 401(k), an IRA, anything.
Which means almost half have nothing set aside in one.
Among families that do have one, the median balance is about one hundred six thousand dollars.
If you have a retirement account, any amount, you're already ahead of nearly half the country.
So why does it feel like everyone is ahead of you?
Reason one: you're seeing highlight reels. People post the new car, not the car loan.
Reason two: you're comparing to averages, and we just saw how averages lie.
Reason three: you're comparing yourself to people who are ten or twenty years further along the curve.
Here's the thing nobody online tells you.
Your position today matters less than your direction.
A twenty-five-year-old with five thousand dollars who saves every month will usually end up far ahead of a forty-year-old with fifty thousand who stopped.
So instead of asking, am I behind, ask three better questions.
One. Do I spend less than I earn? Even by a little.
Two. Do I have a small cushion for emergencies? Even one month is a real start.
Three. Am I investing something every month? Even fifty dollars counts.
If you can say yes to those three, you're on the right path, whatever your number is today.
And here's the only comparison that actually matters: you versus you, a year ago.
Write down your net worth today. Check it again in twelve months. Is it going up? That's the whole game.
Let's recap.
Averages lie. The median family is worth about two hundred sixteen thousand, not a million.
Under thirty-five, the median is about thirty-three thousand. The typical family has about eight thousand in cash.
Almost half carry credit card debt, and almost half have no retirement account.
You're probably not behind. And even if you are, direction beats position.
If you want the exact order of steps to start building from zero, watch my video on starting from zero dollars next.
These numbers are from the Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances. This is education, not financial advice.
